description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 2 on t/op/sprintf2.t:826-880).

THREE measured divergences in one conversion.  t6b's probe H5 found `%a`
AGREES for 1.0, 0.5 and both subnormals it tried, which is why the file's rows
looked like "the file's own shape" -- they are not; these are the shapes it
does not agree on.

  1. ROUNDING IS HALF-UP; perl rounds HALF-TO-EVEN.

        sprintf "%.1a", 0x1.08p+0    perl 0x1.0p+0   PCL 0x1.1p+0
        sprintf "%.1a", 0x1.18p+0    perl 0x1.2p+0   PCL 0x1.3p+0
        sprintf "%.1a", 0x1.28p+0    perl 0x1.2p+0   PCL 0x1.3p+0

     Every exact half in the file's ladder (rows 1537-1557) goes the wrong
     way; the non-half cases (0x1.10, 0x1.17, 0x1.19, 0x1.1f) all AGREE, which
     is what identifies the rule.

  2. AFTER ROUNDING, PCL RE-NORMALISES; perl keeps the exponent.

        sprintf "%.1a", 0x1.f8p+0    perl 0x2.0p+0   PCL 0x1.0p+1
        sprintf "%.2a", 0x1.fffp+0   perl 0x2.00p+0  PCL 0x1.00p+1
        sprintf "%.2a", 0xf.fffp+0   perl 0x2.00p+3  PCL 0x1.00p+4

  3. A SUBNORMAL loses mantissa bits, and the smallest ones read as ZERO.

        sprintf "%a", 3e-322   perl 0x1.e8p-1069  PCL 0x1.ep-1069
        sprintf "%a", 7e-322   perl 0x1.1cp-1067  PCL 0x1.1ap-1067
        sprintf "%a", 3e-324   perl 0x1p-1074     PCL 0x0p+0

     (The 3e-324 rows are perl-side TODOs about denorm LITERALS, but PCL
     diverges from perl's actual output all the same.)

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/sprintf2.t 1512 1514 1516 1517 1522
1524 1529 1537 1543 1545 1547 1549 1551 1553 1555 1557 1558 1563 1564.

SHAPE: one formatter, `%a`'s mantissa/exponent renderer.  1 and 2 are the same
piece of code (round, then decide whether to carry into the exponent); 3 is
the subnormal decomposition and may be a LITERAL-reading problem rather than a
formatting one -- probe `sprintf "%a", 3e-324` against
`sprintf "%a", 5e-324` and against the value built by arithmetic before
deciding.  See also `docs/not-supported.md` "Hex floating-point literals".
subject: `%a` HEX FLOAT: the rounding is half-UP and re-normalises after it, and a SUBNORMAL loses mantissa bits (17 rows of t/op/sprintf2.t)
